title: PPE Compliance Checklist
subtitle: A field-level checklist for verifying PPE availability, condition, and use
intro: Personal protective equipment only protects workers when it is available, in good condition, and actually worn correctly. This checklist gives inspectors a practical sequence for verifying PPE compliance on site, from issue and condition through hazard-specific requirements and training.

sections.title: PPE Availability & Issue
items: Is the required PPE for each task defined and communicated to workers?
Is PPE readily available at point of use or issue stations?
Are stock levels sufficient to replace damaged or worn items without delay?
Is there a documented record of PPE issued to each employee?
Are visitors and contractors issued appropriate PPE before entering the site?

sections.title: PPE Condition & Inspection
items: Is PPE visually inspected for damage or wear before each use?
Are damaged or expired items removed from circulation immediately?
Are PPE inspection dates and results recorded?
Is PPE stored correctly when not in use to avoid degradation?
Are manufacturer expiry or service-life dates checked and enforced?

sections.title: PPE Usage Compliance
items: Are workers wearing the correct PPE for the task and area they are in?
Are PPE-mandatory zones clearly signed at entry points?
Is PPE worn correctly, not just present (e.g. straps fastened, visors down)?
Are non-compliance instances observed, recorded, and corrected on the spot?
Is there visible supervisory enforcement of PPE requirements?

sections.title: Head, Eye & Face Protection
items: Are hard hats worn in all designated head-protection zones?
Are hard hats free of cracks, dents, or degradation from UV exposure?
Is eye and face protection matched to the specific hazard (impact, chemical, welding)?
Are safety glasses or face shields worn during grinding, cutting, or chemical handling tasks?

sections.title: Hearing & Respiratory Protection
items: Is hearing protection worn in areas exceeding the defined noise threshold?
Is the hearing protection's rated attenuation appropriate for the measured noise level?
Is respiratory protection selected based on a documented exposure assessment?
Have workers using respirators been fit-tested for the specific model issued?
Are respirator filters and cartridges replaced according to the manufacturer schedule?

sections.title: Hand & Foot Protection
items: Is glove type matched to the specific hazard (cut, chemical, thermal, electrical)?
Are gloves inspected for punctures, tears, or chemical degradation before use?
Are safety boots worn in all designated foot-protection areas?
Do safety boots meet the required rating (impact, puncture, electrical, slip resistance) for the task?

sections.title: PPE Training & Competency
items: Have workers been trained on correct fitting, use, and limitations of issued PPE?
Is PPE training refreshed at a defined interval or after incidents?
Can workers explain why specific PPE is required for their task?
Are new employees issued and trained on PPE before starting work?
Are training records available and up to date for all employees on site?

sections.title: PPE Storage & Maintenance
items: Is PPE storage clean, dry, and free from contamination sources?
Is reusable PPE cleaned or decontaminated according to a defined procedure?
Are PPE storage areas clearly labelled and organised by type?
Is a maintenance schedule followed for equipment such as respirators and fall-arrest harnesses?

sections.title: Non-Conformance & Replacement
items: Is there a defined process for reporting lost, damaged, or non-conforming PPE?
Are replacement requests actioned within a reasonable timeframe?
Are recurring PPE non-conformances logged and linked to corrective actions?
Are trends in PPE non-conformance reviewed to identify systemic issues?
